answer: PR #15 is a mechanical topology rename (product-control/capabilities -> registry/capability-templates) covering CLI defaults, ADR/spec/doc references, three renamed YAML template artifacts, and registry rows. No new code paths, no new trust-boundary crossings, no new privileged executor, no new network/IO surface, no secrets, no tenant data. The dev-cli template loaders (foundry_capability_schema_gates.rs, foundry_eval_gates.rs) keep the same parse + schema-check logic; only the default PathBuf string changes. The prior trust model (capability YAML -> schema gate -> eval gate -> Cedar policy -> runtime gate per ADR-0007 + audit emission per ADR-0003) is preserved verbatim because the underlying parsers, schema (registry/quality/capability-record.schema.json), and validation invariants are unchanged. ADR-0003/0007/0019/0050/0052 amendments are path-string substitutions; no security carve-out, no policy weakening, no autonomy-tier change, no evidence-contract relaxation. The new registry/capability-templates/ does not collapse previously separated trust boundaries -- product-control/ and registry/ were already inside the same repo trust zone (control-plane data, CI-validated, signed at publish). Verdict: APPROVE from F7 lens.
key_claims: Path-rename only: no new code, no new trust-boundary crossing, no new privileged path.
dev-cli loaders preserve identical parse + schema validation logic; only default PathBuf string moved.
Capability YAML records continue to validate against registry/quality/capability-record.schema.json (unchanged).

ADR-0003 audit-chain contract intact: evidence_emission_topic field, runtime guard, and oya-governance-evidence-contract CI lane still enforced -- the lane's trigger path is updated to registry/capability-templates/ but enforcement semantics are identical.
ADR-0007 Cedar authoritative policy + persona tier model intact: cedar_policy path string moved, but file-loading, policy-authority, and runtime-gate enforcement are unchanged.
ADR-0050 automation-first + ADR-0052 inventory: documentation-only path updates, no carve-out.
No secrets, API keys, tokens, passwords, or credentials introduced in the diff (only PR-15 author own 'secret-store' CLI flag mention is pre-existing).
Supply chain unchanged: no new dependency, no new Cargo.toml edit, no new toolchain surface.
Audit-chain emission entry appended to evidence/audit-chain.jsonl (multispectrum_evidence_attached) -- additive append-only, consistent with ADR-0003 chain shape.

Three renamed template artifacts (capability-record-template.yaml, capability-record-template-v2.yaml, capability-eval-set-template.yaml) inherit prior trust model 1:1 -- they remain curated control-plane inputs validated by capability-schema-validator and foundry-eval gates.
uncertainty_areas: Whether any external lane name or downstream gate trigger filter (e.g. path-based CI workflow include lists) still references the old product-control/ path; the diff updates ADR/doc strings but not necessarily every .github workflow filter -- a stale path filter would silently skip the lane on PRs touching the new directory.

Whether the old product-control/capabilities/ directory is fully removed at HEAD (no shadow YAMLs left that could be loaded preferentially) -- the diff is registry-additive; physical removal of old dir verified only via PR description, not the diff hunk listing.

Whether registry/quality/capability-record.schema.json $schema/$id values were touched (diff does not include this file -- assumed unchanged; if they were drifted, schema validation could degrade silently).

findings.location: CI workflow path filters (not in diff)
findings.blast_radius: If a downstream workflow's `paths:` filter still names `product-control/**`, that lane silently no-ops on PRs that only touch registry/capability-templates/**, weakening gate coverage. Not an attack vector by itself but degrades defense-in-depth.
findings.issue: Topology rename did not surface a search for every CI path filter referencing the old directory. Risk is silent gate skipping, not direct compromise.
findings.remediation: Run `rg -n 'product-control' .github/ ci/ registry/ Justfile Makefile` and confirm zero stale path filters before sunset of product-control/. If any remain, add to follow-up.
findings.remediation_example:
# In CI workflow:
# BAD (stale filter)
on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ['product-control/**']
# GOOD
on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ['registry/capability-templates/**']

findings.owasp_category: A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures (informational)
findings.exploitability: Repo-internal; requires write access to control-plane data.
findings.blast_radius: Capability records remain authoritative inputs to Cedar policy + autonomy tier + audit-emission contract. Centralizing them under registry/ tightens (not loosens) ownership boundaries because registry/ is already covered by active-artifact-contract gate which is run in this PR's verification.
findings.issue: Centralization is net-positive for integrity: one validated location reduces the chance of an orphan/shadow capability YAML escaping validation. No carve-out detected.
findings.remediation: Confirm physical removal of old product-control/capabilities/ at merge time so no shadow capability YAMLs remain loadable.
findings.remediation_example:
# After merge, in a sweep PR:
git rm -r product-control/capabilities/ # if non-empty
# CI lane: gate validate active-artifact-contract should fail if old path still resolves.
